guidebook.intro: Say how you feel and comfort others. Many feelings are said as “I have”: I have sadness, I have anger.

tips.title: Feelings are states
body: Some feelings are past-tense verbs, because you have “become” that way: **Nshemereirwe** (I’m happy), **Nduhire** (I’m tired), **Natiina** (I’m scared).
Others use **nyine**: **Nyine eshaari** (I’m sad, literally “I have sadness”), **Nyine ekiniga** (I’m angry), **Nyine obwoba** (I’m afraid).

tips.title: Two kinds of sorry
body: **Ihangane** is sympathy: “be strong”, said when something bad happens to someone. **Mbabarira** or **Nsaasira** is an apology: “forgive me”.

culture.title: Showing sympathy
body: When someone is sad or has lost a loved one, visitors come to sit with them. **Ihangane** (be strong) is said again and again.
